question: Does the VIL San Nicolas Shoal project documentation provide fish taxa that can be assigned to individual Cavite municipalities, waterbodies, or fishing stations?

method.eprmpAccess: Reviewed the official EMB search-indexed table of contents and excerpts for the 2022 EPRMP. Direct PDF opening returned HTTP 403; the full report and Table 4-32 values were not independently retrieved.
method.hearingReportAccess: Reviewed the official EMB-hosted Public Hearing Report text for the fisheries profile, fishery list, gear-post table, and marine-ecology context (printed pages 96–98).
method.comparison: Compared the source descriptions with nearby 2021 Avalar and Cavite reclamation EIS research reviews. The VIL document is a different proponent/project and has a later baseline date; shared coast and overlapping names do not establish that the catches or datasets are independent.
method.samplingContext: The hearing report describes a marine-ecology baseline across coastal waters of Rosario, Naic, Tanza, Noveleta, and Ternate during 26–28 November 2021. It reports twelve spot dives, eight manta-tow pathways, and fishing-gear mapping at posts 1–18. Its fishery table separately groups names across fishing grounds of Rosario, Naic, Noveleta, Tanza, and Cavite City.
method.tableCaution: The report does not crosswalk the grouped fish-list rows to the 12 spot dives, 18 gear posts, a named municipality, a waterbody, a catch date, or a specimen. The EPRMP table-of-contents entry for Table 4-32 advertises gear types and catch-per-unit-effort during the 26–28 November 2021 assessment, but those values were not visible in the accessible indexed excerpt and are not inferred.
method.rightsAndImages: No item-specific reuse license for the EPRMP/PHR tables, photos, or maps was verified. The PHR includes specimen photographs, but no image was independently matched for Bangwit and none was copied or used.

sourceSummary.report: The PHR fishery list contains 23 name rows; three rows are crustacean labels and several entries are genus-level rather than species-level.
sourceSummary.localityScope: The fish-list caption pools grounds from five named coastal LGUs. The five-municipality 2021 marine assessment area and gear posts are not a fish-taxon-by-station matrix.
sourceSummary.fieldContext: Gear-post observations and the EPRMP Table 4-32 title establish a fishing-gear/effort mapping activity, not a site-specific species inventory.

taxonomicReviewNeeds: The table presents English, local, and scientific-name columns, but no specimen or image crosswalk is supplied for the fish-list rows.

The source pairs “Spotted scat” and “Kitang” with Gerres filamentosus, while another “Spadefish” row also uses “Kitang” with Scatophagus argus; preserve the printed labels and resolve the pairing against an authoritative taxonomy and source specimens before use.
Stolephorus sp., Upeneus species, and Siganus species remain genus-level labels; do not promote them to species names.
Acetes, Metapenaeus ensis, and Portunus armatus are non-fish labels within the table; do not count all 23 rows as fish species.
findings.overlapAssessment: This VIL project has its own 2021 baseline and is separate from the Avalar and Island D reclamation EIS projects. The fish list is nevertheless broad and pooled, and the documents provide no survey lineage or catch-level crosswalk to establish independent species confirmations. Keep project records distinct and do not sum their names as unique regional occurrences.
findings.waterbodyCaution: The project and its gear maps describe offshore/coastal work in Manila Bay and adjacent Cavite LGU waters. They do not define legal municipal-water boundaries, capture locations for the fish-list rows, or the extent of Tanza Marine Tree Park.

decision.disposition: Retain the VIL EPRMP/PHR as a distinct historical Cavite fishery research lead only. The pooled fish list, gear posts, and marine-ecology stations have no verified taxon-to-site crosswalk. Keep source labels untranscribed in this access/scope review until their names, station allocation, provenance, and reuse scope can be checked.

nonClaims: The pooled table does not prove that every listed fish was caught in each named municipality or at any individual gear post.
The EPRMP Table 4-32 title does not establish unreviewed CPUE values, species-specific catch rates, or a fish-to-gear mapping.
The project field period does not date the source fish-list rows individually or establish current fish presence.
The report does not establish a complete Cavite/Manila Bay checklist, diet, bait effectiveness, fishing access, safety, legal boundaries, or current regulations.
Fish photographs in the hearing report are not authorized Bangwit reference images without identification and item-specific reuse review.
nextActions: Continue with freshwater and brackish Cavite sources; do not let coastal EIS lists substitute for Cañas, Labac, Ylang-Ylang, or other inland-water evidence.
Review the VIL fish-list labels against accepted taxonomy as a separate task while preserving the table text and unresolved common-name pairings.
Seek public, readable values for Table 4-32 and source documentation for Table 4-31; retain the current access and locality limits if no accessible record appears.

sources.supports: Official EMB-indexed 2022 EPRMP contents identifying Tables 4-31 and 4-32 and the assessment dates; direct PDF access failed, so Table 4-32 values were not reviewed.
Official EMB Public Hearing Report full-text excerpts for the 23-row pooled fishery list, survey context, and 18 gear posts; no fish-taxon-to-site crosswalk is provided.
